text:
前几天又聊到语音输入法

评论区有朋友说网易的叭哥说不错，试了一下，确实可以！

网易在 AI 领域最近做这些小产品都很不错，这个叭哥说，还有 UU 远程都非常好。

它这个是免费的，像 Typeless 还是就海外很多都是收费的.

他们用到的这个本地的模型也是他们自己训的 ASR 模型。

我主要是在桌面端将语音输入法和正常的输入法分开，这样的话就不会相互影响.

正常输入法有语音的时候，因为输入法切换什么的，经常会被打断，然后你输出一长串，最后又被打断没了。

这个就很麻烦，后分开的话就可以避免这个问题。

然后国产的这种语音输入法有个什么好处呢？就是它速度快呀。老快了，这个速度。

他们这个也没有什么多余功能，非常克制，就是一个输入，然后还有一个翻译，没有什么花里胡哨的一个界面，进去就直接用。

然后润色，比如说 Typeless 的润色啊，真的很烦。

每次尤其是这种模型名称、数字之类的，他固执地认为 Claude 的模型就只有到 3.5，模型名称和一些数字上就要给我故意改错，就我说的很清楚，他也会改错。

然后叭哥说就没有这个问题。他掌握得很好，不会过度润色。

自定义词库也有，因为我有自己的 Memory ，我直接让 Codex 分析了一下我的 Memory，给我出了一个自定义词库的文件，直接上传就全部搞好了。

这段也都是叭哥说语音输入的。

For two decades, writing the exploit was the bottleneck in a cyberattack. AI made that step cheap, and patching hasn't gotten faster:

- On average, attacks went from landing 63 days after disclosure in 2018-19 to 7 days before it in 2025

- A working exploit went from a skilled person's month to a few hours of machine time

- The median time to fully fix a known-exploited bug rose to 43 days

a16z's @asaf_ez and @steph_zhang expect a long, expensive worm era, hitting hardest where systems can't update fast: hospitals, schools, small water systems.

"When attacking is nearly free, attackers no longer need to want a target."

Full piece from Asaf Ezra and Steph Zhang: https://www.a16z.news/p/the-exploit-was-the-bottleneck

Figma CFO Praveer Melwani used to spend his days writing hundreds of lines of SQL just to get one set of numbers everyone trusted. Now his finance team builds its own AI tools to do that work.

He sees the CFO's job shifting from traffic cop to business enabler, as long as the people doing the building still own their thinking.

Praveer joins a16z's Seema Amble and Ivan Makarov, authors of "You Need a New CFO," to discuss the growth-stage finance team that built 40 to 50 agents in a month or two, what breaks when every rep vibe codes their own dashboard, and how finance went from sitting out hackathons to winning them.

Figma CFO Praveer Melwani says his corp dev team now tests a target's moat by trying to vibe code its product, then runs the M&A memo past AI versions of Figma's leaders:

"I think our team's gotten really damn good at some of this. You can get through some of the, you know, 'Is this a real thing? Is it not? How difficult is it or not?' There's obviously nuances to a whole bunch of these ideas, but it gives you like a solid intuition there."

"More often than not, there are themes, there are similar questions, there are ways that we all as leaders tend to have a way of looking at problems. And what's been interesting is [the corp dev team has] gone and created unique [AI] personalities for each of us as leaders... that they can go and run their investment memos by."

"They'll sit there kind of going back and forth and saying, 'Okay, this is what Praveer would say, and this is what [CEO] Dylan would say, and this is what Sean would say,' our CRO... It reduces the cycle time that we're all sitting together on."
